summary.text: A 61-year-old black woman diagnosed with HIV in 2002 remained on initial antiretroviral therapy for 16 years with suppressed viral load and CD4 counts above 600. In January 2018 she presented with progressive anemia and mental depression and the regimen was switched.

In September 2018 she developed severe anemia and thrombocytopenia with transfusion dependency; parvovirus B19 PCR was negative. Bone marrow showed multilineage dysplasia with 5% blasts, karyotype with trisomy 8 confirmed by FISH, and an ASXL1 exon 12 mutation, and she was diagnosed with MDS-EB-1 at very high risk.

Supportive care with ART, transfusions, erythropoietin and one cycle of azacitidine was without improvement. Seven months later the karyotype demonstrated clonal evolution, and FISH identified cells with both trisomy 8 and trisomy 21. Hemoglobin was 3.5 g/dL and platelets 7 x 10^(9)/L with circulating myeloblasts, and she died in July 2019.
